(1) Who compiled the manuscript, and where it was when this edition was made — stated as an inference, not a fact. 「藩制一覽表九册ハ、舊修史局ニ於テ、集録編纂シタルモノノ如ク、原本ハ目下内閣記録課ニ所藏ス。」 The survey runs to nine fascicles; the compilers of this printed edition say it "appears to be" (ノノ如ク) something collected and compiled at the former Bureau of Historiography, and that the original was then held by the Cabinet Records Section. The hedge is theirs — they did not know with certainty who assembled it. The nine-fascicle count agrees with the project's own reading of the source's structure.

(2) The original is a working draft carrying later editorial layers. 「其ノ書修史局ノ罫紙ヲ用ヰ、朱字ヲ以テ書入ヲナシ、或ハ符箋ヲ爲シ、或ハ其局編修員ノ私考ヲ追記スル所アリテ、體裁一見稿本ノ如シ。」 The manuscript is written on the Bureau of Historiography's own ruled paper; insertions were made in vermilion ink; slips of paper were attached in places; and in places the Bureau's compilers added their own private opinions. The compilers therefore say the thing looks at first sight like a draft manuscript (稿本). This is the caveat that matters most for using the figures: some of what stands on a page of the original came from the Bureau's staff rather than from the domain that filed the return.

(3) Who ordered the survey, what was to be reported, who supplied it, and over what window. 「本書ハ明治初年、太政官ガ各藩ニ向テ其藩ノ草高、税目、税額、人口、戸數、社寺數ノ調査ヲ命セシニ對シテ、明治二、三年ニ亘リ、各藩ヨリ上申セシモノヲ」 The Dajōkan issued the order, in the early years of Meiji, to each domain. The named categories are kusadaka, tax items, tax amounts, population, household counts, and shrine-and-temple counts. The returns were filed by the domains themselves (各藩ヨリ上申) — self-reported, not measured by the centre. And they came in across Meiji 2 and 3 (1869 and 1870), so the survey has a two-year window rather than a single as-of date; the printed 二 and 三 are separated by a punctuation mark, which I confirmed in the row-projection (二 at rows 1871-1936, 、 at 1949-1966, 三 at 1977-2048).

So the list of surveyed categories may be extended there, and the officials and military data that fill fascicles 8 and 9 are not among the six categories named here. The faint rectangular stamp is illegible even under autocontrast at 2x; I did not attempt to read it.

Page is not blank. COUNT. Column detection on each of the four bands separately returns 13 columns each (upper names centred at x 945, 1080, 1215, 1349, 1484, 1618, 1750, 1883, 2019, 2154, 2288, 2425, 2562; upper numbers at 933…2551; lower names at 928…2546; lower numbers at 917…2534). Each number column sits about 11 px left of its name column, so the name-to-number pairing by rank is correct and no line is dropped or doubled. 13 + 13 = 26, matching the 26 claimed entries.

NAMES. I read all 26 at 3x in six crops (top_names_R/M/L, bot_names_R/M/L) and went to 8–12x on the look-alikes: 島 in 矢島藩 (白 block above a full-width 山 — 島, not 嶋), 島 in 眞島藩 (same), 丸 in 丸龜藩 (a vertical tick rises above the crossing stroke with a separate short stroke to its right; 九 has neither), 龜 in 丸龜藩 (kyujitai, left-side prongs and 乚 base), 嶺 in 松嶺藩 (山 stacked above 領), 鞠 in 鞠山藩 (革 + 匊), 川 in 松川藩 (three separate verticals, no base stroke), 櫛 and 羅 in 櫛羅藩. I checked this on the facing half-leaf: lower_p009_right.jpg carries the margin number 十 (10) and indexes pages 363–381; this leaf carries 十一 (11) and indexes 383–403. Two halves of one physical leaf carrying 10 and 11 means the printed marginal series counts pages, not leaves, and the entry numbers belong to that same series. Corrected gloss below.

黑川藩. At 14x with autocontrast the upper component is inked shut. Two light spots sit on a diagonal inside it, not the 2x2 grid of white cells that 里 would give, which favours the kyujitai 黑; I cannot settle it from this scan and the note should say so rather than resting on print size alone.

It is incomplete in a way that could mislead. In the Vol1 fascicle-5 sequence the corresponding slot is filled: 松尾藩 pdf 212, 眞島藩 213, 松嶺藩 214, 守山藩 215, 敦賀藩 216, 松岡藩 217 — positionally identical to this index's 松尾 399, 眞島 400, 松嶺 401, 松川 402, 鞠山 402, 松岡 403, and HI_pdf_bookmark_index.csv itself labels that 敦賀藩 row "鞠山藩 — Tsuruga". I did not open the Vol2 data page for book page 402 to see which domain heading is printed there, and I did not check any published han list to confirm whether 松川藩 is a later name of 守山藩. The 黑/黒 reading remains unresolved at this scan resolution.

A row-projection scan over the whole leaf found a horizontal rule at y = 2414 and, below it, a second tier of exactly 4 name columns (x = 2197-2657) and 4 number columns (x = 2203-2651), again aligned pairwise. I then cropped each column and read it at 3x-14x with autocontrast.

Layout. The leaf is one page of the table of contents, set in two horizontal tiers, each read right to left: the upper tier runs the full width with 13 entries (pages 461-469), the rule divides the leaf, and the lower tier holds only 4 entries at the right-hand end (pages 470-472), the rest of that tier being blank because the index ends here. The left margin carries the running head 目次 (x = 881-932, two characters set apart vertically) and, lower down, the folio number 十五 (page 15 of the front matter). The right margin and the space between the rule and the lower tier are blank - I checked both by ink count over the paper area.

No fascicle heading is printed on this half-leaf. I did not find a 藩制一覧表第N line anywhere on it, so I have left the fascicle field empty on every entry. I have not opened the earlier mokuji leaves, so I cannot say which heading governs this block from the printed page; the internal evidence (book pages 461-472, which map to the officials-and-military pages at the end of volume 2) points to 第九, but that is inference, not something printed here, so I did not record it.

Ordering check. Cross-check against the transcribed data. Treating the reprint's printed page as 2 x pdf_page - 24 for a right half-leaf and - 23 for a left one, every one of the 17 entries lands on the volume-2 PDF page where MASTER_hansei_ichiran.csv or HI_pdf_bookmark_index.csv already places that domain's fascicle-9 block, within one half-leaf: 母里 469 -> pdf 246 L (MASTER has 母里 on 246 L), 森 and 守山 468 -> 246 R (MASTER has both on 246 R), 盛岡 467 -> 245 L (MASTER 245 L), 一橋 and 日出 466 -> 245 R (MASTER 245 R), 關宿 471 -> 247 L (MASTER 247 L), 須坂 472 -> 248 R (MASTER 248 R). I measured ink-column centres with a projection scan: the upper register has 14 name columns (the rightmost, at x≈2316, is the header column, not an entry) and 13 number columns; the lower register has 13 name columns and 13 number columns. Name and number centres match one-to-one within 5 px in both registers, so the pairings below are measured, not eyeballed.

The header column carries the running head 目次 in the upper register (目 at y 1313-1360, 次 at y 1566-1614) and the leaf's own index page number 十四 (= 14) in the lower register (y 3133-3234). No 藩制一覧表第N fascicle heading is printed anywhere on this leaf, so the fascicle field is omitted on every entry. A full-page ink-row scan (threshold <150, x 300-2700) returned only the two name bands, the two number bands, the rule, the two header glyphs and two dust specks — nothing above the first name band and nothing between the registers.

Page numbers are three kanji each, not two. I cropped and upscaled both number bands to confirm: upper register 四四四 through 四五二 (444-452), lower register 四五三 through 四六〇 (453-460). The two registers run continuously, 452 to 453.

The listing is in iroha order, which independently corroborates the readings: the upper register runs through the み group (ミヤヅ, ミナクチ, ミブ, ミカヅキ, ミネヤマ, ミカミ, ミッカイチ, ミヤガハ, ミネヲカ, ミクサ, ミイケ) and then opens the し group with 靜岡 (シヅオカ) and 新發田 (シバタ); the lower register is all し until the final line 廣島 (ヒロシマ), which opens the ひ group. In iroha, み precedes し and し precedes ひ.

Three readings I zoomed on individually at 5-8x with autocontrast and unsharp masking:
- The fourth line of the upper register prints 三月日藩, with 月 above 日. That is a transposition in the original type for 三日月藩 (Mikazuki), which is how MASTER_hansei_ichiran.csv records the domain. I transcribed what is printed and flagged it.
- Both mine- lines print 峰 with 山 as a left-side radical, not 峯 with 山 stacked on top: 峰山藩 and 峰岡藩. MASTER records these two as 峯山藩 and 峯岡藩, so the index and the body transcription differ in this one glyph.
- 新莊藩 prints 莊 (艹 over 爿 + 土), confirmed at 8x. MASTER records 新庄藩.

I also checked every name in this index against the 302 domain names in MASTER_hansei_ichiran.csv. All match except the four just noted and 三上藩, which has no entry in MASTER at all — worth flagging as a possible gap in the body transcription rather than a misread here, since the glyphs 三 / 上 / 藩 are unambiguous and the iroha position (ミカミ) fits.

One glyph I could not resolve: the first character of 靜岡藩. At this scan resolution the bottom of the left component cannot be separated into 円 (靑, giving 靜) versus 月 (青, giving 静). I transcribed 靜岡藩 because the volume uses kyūjitai throughout on this leaf (廣, 發, 莊, 島), but MASTER records 静岡藩 and this line should not be treated as a confirmed mismatch.

proposal.reasoning: The leaf is the 奥付 of the lower volume, printed as a single ruled rectangle set in the lower-centre of an otherwise empty half-leaf. Nothing else appears on the sheet — no library stamp, no page number, no table data. I read the full-resolution scan (3094 x 4489) and then cropped and upscaled six regions with PIL to check every column: the two date columns at the right, the boxed title cartouche and the boxed 非賣品 slug, the 編輯者 column with its address, the 發行者 column, the 印刷者 column, and the 發行所 column with the telephone and postal-transfer numbers. Layout inside the box, right to left: (1) 昭和四年一月二十日印刷; (2) 昭和四年一月廿五日發行; (3) a dotted-frame seal reading 不許覆製, set high and to the left of the date columns; (4) a thin ruled cartouche reading 藩制一覽表下卷, with a second small ruled box to its left reading 非賣品; then the four responsibility columns, each with its address printed in smaller type in the column to the right of the name. Two things I could not settle and have not guessed at. First, the third character of the title — the ink is filled in solid at this resolution and the 覽 / 覧 distinction cannot be resolved; I transcribed it as 覽 because every other character in the box is set in the pre-1946 form (發, 會, 豐, 圓, 區, 橋, 賣, 籍, 輯, 覆, 製), so the old form is the consistent reading, but the glyph itself is not legible enough to prove it. Second, no series name is printed anywhere in the box — the publisher 日本史籍協會 is named as the issuing body, but the words 日本史籍協會叢書 do not appear — so I left publication_data.series empty rather than supplying the series title from outside knowledge. Kanji numerals checked against the reading guide: 二十日 = the 20th (print date), 廿五日 = the 25th (issue date), 四百十八番地 = lot 418, 三二八七 and 三九四五 read as digit strings, not as sums. No price is printed; the book is marked 非賣品, not for sale.
